traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.25, 0.2, 0.15], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Salix lasiandra: grows 5 m to 15 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Salix lasiandra: leaves 6 cm to 10 cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Salix lasiandra: leaves 1.5 cm to 3.5 cm wide.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Salix lasiandra (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.41 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 5 records in 3 sources); trunks 0.41, branches 0.44. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Fryer 2015, Salix lucida including subsp. lasiandra, read): no age is known for shining willow itself, but Salix seedlings usually first produce seeds at 5 to 10 years, sprouts at 1 or 2. The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Salix, read) gives 5 to 10 years for seedlings. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of broadleaf's default of 4 years.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a many-stemmed tree with an open, irregular crown and alternate, long-pointed, glossy, finely toothed leaves. Not fitted to measurements. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 10 m tall at 25 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: glossy green leaves; dark, furrowed bark. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): dark grey-brown bark furrowed into flat interlacing ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): a sun-loving willow whose leaves change little with light; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2918186), as no source read gives it.

traits.life_span.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2918186), as no source read gives it.

generator.params.bloom_area.note: The leaf area its `bloom` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows, now that the look follows the species' stated facts (was 0.050).

traits.leaf_apex.note: FNA, Salix lasiandra (read 2026-10-18): the largest mid-shoot blades taper to a caudate to acuminate tip.
